facts.text: The official Vera Rubin datasheet rates the NVL72 rack at 227 kW (MaxP), 187 kW (MaxQ) and 156 kW (MaxLPS), for a 45 °C coolant inlet — 72 Rubin GPUs and 36 Vera CPUs per rack

Rubin described as the world's first 100% liquid-cooled platform — every chip and networking component cooled entirely by liquid, "no fans anywhere in the system"; PG25 coolant (75% water / 25% propylene glycol) enters at up to 45 °C and exits ~55 °C, enabling chiller-less dry-cooler heat rejection with near-zero water consumption

faq.q: Why is NVIDIA pushing data centers to liquid cooling?
faq.a: Rack density: GB200 NVL72 needs ~120 kW per rack, GB300 NVL72 up to 142 kW, and NVIDIA's datasheet rates the Vera Rubin NVL72 at up to 227 kW (MaxP) — beyond air. Vera Rubin NVL72 goes fully liquid: 100% liquid-cooled, no fans anywhere in the system, PG25 coolant entering at up to 45 °C so heat can be rejected by dry coolers with near-zero water.

faq.q: What coolant do NVIDIA racks use?
faq.a: PG25 — 75% water / 25% propylene glycol. NVIDIA's Vera Rubin program runs it in closed loops with inlets up to 45 °C (facility water ~41 °C to the CDUs) and rates it for up to 10 years in a closed loop.

productLines.note: Immersion tank paired with OCP-recognized MiTAC hyperconverged servers: >100 kW dissipation, 45U or 22U, 19" or 21" OCP support, 1.03 PUE, zero water waste — listed in the OCP Marketplace

facts.text: Surpassed 500 MW of liquid-cooled infrastructure deployed and expanded into data center Design & Build services (Rubix), marking 10 years as a company; CleanSpark selected Submer as its first strategic partner for AI data center expansion in North America
Closed a $55.5M all-equity growth round led by M&G with Planet First Partners participating; launched SmartPod EXO the same year

profiles.ocp: Developed the SmartPod OCP Open Rack v3 immersion pod in collaboration with OCP; SmartPod + MiTAC solution listed in the OCP Marketplace; participant in OCP immersion cooling proof-of-concept work.

faq.q: What is Submer's largest immersion pod?
faq.a: SmartPod EXO — up to 361 kW per pod with 2N pump/CDU redundancy, taking 50RU of 19"/21" gear or 47OU of OCP ORv3, and running hot water up to 60 °C to enable free cooling and heat reuse.

faq.q: How much immersion cooling has Submer deployed?
faq.a: The company states it surpassed 500 MW of liquid-cooled infrastructure deployed in 2025, its tenth year, and presented multi-GW full-chain case studies with CleanSpark among its North American partners.

profiles.name: GRC (Green Revolution Cooling)
profiles.tagline: Austin-based pioneer of single-phase immersion cooling — ElectroSafe-fluid ICEraQ rack systems, containerized ICEtank data centers, and since 2025 direct-liquid-cooling CDUs.

productLines.name: ICEraQ (SX / Flex / Micro)
productLines.note: Single-phase immersion rack systems with integrated CDU — supports up to 368 kW IT load; company claims up to 95% lower cooling energy

productLines.name: ICEraQ Nano
productLines.note: 10U liquid-to-air edge immersion rack, up to 13 kW, no chilled water required — launched November 2025

productLines.name: ReliaSys IR500 CDU
productLines.note: Up to 500 kW coolant distribution unit for direct liquid cooling and rear-door heat exchangers — launched November 2025

productLines.name: ElectroSafe fluids
productLines.note: Proprietary single-phase dielectric coolant line used across GRC immersion systems

facts.text: UNICOM Engineering and GRC launched fully integrated immersion-cooled AI solutions for evaluation, deployment and industrial-scale adoption
Samsung Ventures invested in GRC and Samsung C&T formed a strategic partnership in its latest funding round; Cisco and GRC formed an engineering alliance on immersion cooling

faq.q: What is GRC's largest immersion system?
faq.a: The ICEraQ single-phase immersion rack family — integrated CDU supporting up to 368 kW IT load. At the other end, the ICEraQ Nano (Nov 2025) is a 10U liquid-to-air edge rack up to 13 kW with no chilled water.

faq.q: Does GRC also make direct-to-chip products?
faq.a: Yes — since November 2025: the ReliaSys IR500 CDU delivers up to 500 kW for direct liquid cooling and rear-door heat exchangers.

profiles.name: Baltimore Aircoil (BAC)
profiles.tagline: Heat rejection for liquid-cooled data centers — cooling towers, hybrid and dry coolers — plus the COBALT single-phase immersion system.
profiles.ownership: Wholly owned subsidiary of Amsted Industries (since 1985)

productLines.name: TrilliumSeries Dry Cooler
productLines.note: Water-free axial-fan dry cooler for water-stressed sites; up to 10,000 MBH (~2.9 MW) per unit, vertical coils, independent fans/VFDs/coils for redundancy

productLines.name: FXV3 Closed Circuit Cooling Tower
productLines.note: Combined-flow closed-circuit tower positioned by BAC for data centers; capacity not published on the product page

productLines.name: HXV Hybrid Cooler
productLines.note: Hybrid wet/dry cooler — BAC cites up to 70% water savings vs traditional fluid coolers and up to 60% more energy efficiency than air-cooled systems

productLines.name: COBALT Immersion Cooling System
productLines.note: Pairs a CorTex single-phase immersion tank (16/32/38/48RU, 19" and 21" servers, PUE up to 1.05 claimed) with BAC outdoor heat rejection

facts.text: Houston colocation deployment: COBALT single-phase immersion with BAC heat rejection ran year-round without mechanical cooling

BAC's CorTex immersion tank certified under the Intel Data Center Certified Solution for Immersion Cooling program for 4th/5th-gen Xeon — program developed with Intel, ExxonMobil, Hypertec and Micron (Dec 2, 2025)
Launched upgraded CorTex-powered immersion tanks (Oct 9, 2025) in 16/32/38/48RU sizes as the indoor half of the COBALT system

profiles.ocp: Listed in the OCP membership directory; no project-level contributions verifiable from public sources.

faq.q: What does BAC make for liquid-cooled data centers?
faq.a: The heat-rejection half of the loop: TrilliumSeries water-free dry coolers (up to 10,000 MBH ≈ 2.9 MW per unit), FXV3 closed-circuit towers, and HXV hybrid coolers (BAC cites up to 70% water savings) — plus the COBALT single-phase immersion system that pairs a CorTex tank with BAC outdoor heat rejection.

faq.q: Are BAC immersion tanks certified?
faq.a: Yes — the CorTex tank was certified (Dec 2025) under the Intel Data Center Certified Solution for Immersion Cooling program for 4th/5th-gen Xeon, a program developed with Intel, ExxonMobil, Hypertec and Micron.

profiles.name: EVAPCO
profiles.tagline: Employee-owned heat-transfer manufacturer — dry coolers, adiabatic and hybrid closed-circuit coolers, and evaporative towers for heat rejection in liquid-cooled data centers.

productLines.name: eco-Air Series APEX (EAW-HD)
productLines.note: CTI-certified, water-free factory-assembled dry cooler for high-density data centers — introduced February 2026 (per-unit kW/MBH figures: not published on the announcement page)

productLines.name: eco-Air Titan
productLines.note: EVAPCO's largest adiabatic cooler for large-scale heat-rejection duty including data centers — announced 2025, fans up to 36 ft diameter

productLines.name: Eco-ATWB-H hybrid closed-circuit cooler
productLines.note: Hybrid dry + evaporative closed-circuit cooler in EVAPCO's data center heat-rejection lineup

productLines.name: Factory-assembled cooling towers
productLines.note: CTI-certified evaporative open-loop towers offered alongside the dry/hybrid lines for data center heat rejection

facts.text: Introduced eco-Air Series APEX — its largest factory-assembled CTI-certified dry cooler for high-density, mission-critical data centers (Feb 2026)
Unveiled eco-Air Titan at AHR Expo 2025 for large-scale heat rejection and announced production expansion in the US, Belgium and China
Announced Taneytown world-headquarters expansion: 45,000 sq ft of office space and 275 new jobs (Maryland Governor's office)

faq.q: What does EVAPCO offer for water-free data center heat rejection?
faq.a: The eco-Air dry cooler line — including the APEX series (introduced Feb 2026, EVAPCO's largest factory-assembled CTI-certified dry cooler) and the Titan adiabatic cooler (2025, fans up to 36 ft) — plus Eco-ATWB-H hybrid units that blend dry and evaporative operation.

profiles.name: Alfa Laval
profiles.tagline: Swedish heat-transfer specialist — brazed and gasketed plate heat exchangers at the core of data center liquid cooling, inside CDUs and in heat-rejection, free-cooling and heat-reuse loops.

productLines.name: Brazed plate heat exchangers
productLines.note: Described as the market's most comprehensive brazed plate line — a custom CB-series unit is the core heat exchanger inside Boyd's 2.3 MW ROL2300 in-row CDU

productLines.name: Gasketed plate-and-frame heat exchangers
productLines.note: Industrial gasketed PHEs for data center free cooling / waterside economizers and heat recovery, with AHRI thermal performance certification offered

productLines.name: Liquid cooling solutions (direct-to-chip and immersion)
productLines.note: Heat-transfer offering spanning direct-to-chip CDU loops and single-phase/two-phase immersion configurations

productLines.name: Self-cleaning filters and strainers
productLines.note: Automatically self-cleaning cylindrical filter baskets protecting heat exchangers from fouling in data center cooling systems

facts.text: An Alfa Laval brazed plate heat exchanger is the core of Boyd's ROL2300 in-row CDU (up to 2.3 MW) — Alfa Laval supplies the heat exchanger; the CDU is Boyd's product
Collaboration with Boyd announced on a direct-to-chip liquid cooling system for ultra-high-density AI/HPC racks
Announced Platinum membership of the Open Compute Project Foundation

profiles.ocp: Platinum member of the Open Compute Project Foundation since 2023.

faq.q: What does Alfa Laval make for liquid cooling?
faq.a: The heat exchangers, not complete CDUs: brazed plate units inside CDUs (a custom CB-series unit sits at the core of Boyd's 2.3 MW ROL2300), gasketed plate-and-frame exchangers for free cooling and heat reuse, plus self-cleaning filters protecting the loops.

faq.q: Is Alfa Laval involved in OCP?
faq.a: Yes — a Platinum member of the Open Compute Project Foundation since 2023.

profiles.name: Schneider Electric
profiles.tagline: Data center physical-infrastructure incumbent turned end-to-end liquid cooling integrator — CDUs, rear doors, cold plates, chillers, controls and micro data centers — anchored by its acquisition of Motivair.

productLines.name: EcoStruxure liquid cooling portfolio (with Motivair)
productLines.note: CDU family scaling 105 kW to 2.5 MW; ChilledDoor rear-door heat exchanger up to 75 kW/rack (Open19/OCP compatible); liquid-to-air HDU rejecting 100 kW in a 600 mm footprint and supporting water loops to 132 kW; dynamic cold plates; chillers and TCS loops

productLines.name: AI Factory reference designs (co-developed with NVIDIA)
productLines.note: Reference designs for liquid-cooled NVIDIA AI clusters: 7.392 MW GB200 NVL72 and 7.536 MW GB300 NVL72 (RD111 supports up to ~227 kW per rack); Sept 2025 designs add integrated power management and liquid cooling controls for NVIDIA Mission Control

productLines.name: EcoStruxure Micro Data Center
productLines.note: All-in-one edge enclosures (6U-42U; sealed R-Series, S-Series, soundproof C-Series) — power, cooling, security and management; pre-validated partner designs at 3-5 kW with Cisco, Dell EMC, HPE, Lenovo; this line is air/enclosure-cooled, not liquid

facts.text: Unveiled its first complete end-to-end liquid cooling portfolio with Motivair (Sept 29): CDUs 105 kW-2.5 MW, thermal performance claimed in 6 of the world's top-10 supercomputers, NVIDIA certification, and Motivair's fourth plant (Buffalo, NY) tripling output

Closed the controlling-stake Motivair acquisition in February 2025 (75% for ~$850M announced Oct 2024, remainder to follow); announced integrated power+cooling-controls reference designs for GB300 NVL72 (Sept 18)

profiles.ocp: ChilledDoor rack-level liquid cooling listed as compatible with Open19/OCP rack standards; formal corporate OCP membership not verified.

faq.q: What did Schneider Electric buy from Motivair?
faq.a: A ~75% controlling stake for ~$850M cash (announced Oct 2024, closed February 2025), with the remainder expected by 2028 — Motivair now operates as 'Motivair by Schneider Electric'.

faq.q: What liquid cooling does Schneider offer?
faq.a: An end-to-end EcoStruxure portfolio built around Motivair: CDUs 105 kW-2.5 MW, ChilledDoor 75 kW rear-door heat exchangers, a 100 kW liquid-to-air HDU, dynamic cold plates, chillers and controls — plus NVIDIA co-developed AI factory reference designs up to ~227 kW per rack.

profiles.name: STULZ
profiles.tagline: Hamburg precision-cooling veteran bridging facility plant and the rack — CyberCool CDUs, an OCP-accepted 2 MW Deschutes CDU, and the liquid-cooled Micro DC cabinet launched with CoolIT.

productLines.name: CyberCool CDU
productLines.note: Coolant distribution units rated 345-1,380 kW across two sizes; facility water 32 °C / technology loop 36 °C for ASHRAE W32-W+ warm-water free cooling; serves liquid-to-chip and immersion loops; 50 µm TCS filtration, sanitary-grade stainless piping

productLines.name: Deschutes CDU (CyberCool Liquid Cooling Distribution Unit)
productLines.note: OCP Accepted CDU built to Google's Deschutes 5.0 specification: 2 MW at 3 °C approach, 500 GPM (1,890 LPM), 80 PSI, N+1 seal-less pumps, 0.2 µm side-stream filtration

productLines.name: Micro DC
productLines.note: Factory-integrated 'server room in a rack': 42U, 600/800 mm widths, IP54/IP55 options; P-series (Prodigy 4-11 kW) or C-series (CyberRow 4-20 kW) cooling with CW, DX, glycol economizer and liquid chip-cooling options

productLines.name: CyberRack SideCooler
productLines.note: Closed-loop water-cooled rack-side unit for edge and micro data centers (launched Sept 2025): installs between racks or inside a Micro DC, hot-swappable fans, high water temperatures for extended free cooling

facts.text: Deschutes CDU listed OCP Accepted (built to Google's Project Deschutes 5.0 spec: 2 MW at 3 °C, 500 GPM); introduced the CyberRack SideCooler for high-density edge racks (Sept 2025)

STULZ and CoolIT Systems launched the liquid-cooled Micro DC for HPC/edge (June 2017) — CoolIT Rack DCLC capturing 60-80% of server heat at chip level with an integrated STULZ unit handling the rest; 48U rack scalable beyond 80 kW of IT load, marketed as the partners' first 'Chip-to-Atmosphere' offering

profiles.ocp: Deschutes CDU (CyberCool Liquid Cooling Distribution Unit) is OCP Accepted and listed in the OCP Marketplace, built to Google's Project Deschutes 5.0 CDU specification. Source: opencompute.org

faq.q: What is STULZ's OCP-accepted CDU?
faq.a: The Deschutes CDU (CyberCool LC distribution unit): 2 MW at 3 °C approach, 500 GPM, 80 PSI, N+1 seal-less pumps — built to Google's Project Deschutes 5.0 specification and listed OCP Accepted.

faq.q: Was the STULZ-CoolIT liquid-cooled micro DC the first of its kind?
faq.a: The partners marketed their 2017 Micro DC as the first 'Chip-to-Atmosphere' offering: CoolIT Rack DCLC cold plates captured 60-80% of server heat while a STULZ precision-cooling unit handled the remainder in a 48U rack scalable beyond 80 kW.

profiles.name: Sugon DataEnergy
profiles.tagline: Beijing-listed, Sugon-affiliated full-stack liquid cooling provider — immersion phase-change (C8000), cold-plate (C7000), CDU/manifold components and modular data centers; first to commercialize immersion phase-change cooling at scale in China.

productLines.name: C8000 series (immersion phase-change)
productLines.note: C8000 V3.0 rack supports >900 kW (MW-class), heat flux >200 W/cm², PUE <1.04 — billed as the world's first MW-class phase-change immersion full-rack solution (April 2026)

productLines.name: C7000 series (cold-plate / air-liquid hybrid)
productLines.note: Cold-plate and wind-liquid hybrid cooling products, including C7000 2.0 and the C7000-F phase-change indirect liquid cooling solution

productLines.name: Cold-plate liquid cooling components
productLines.note: CDU (liquid heat-exchange unit), VCDU vertical flow-distribution manifolds, prefabricated piping systems and cold-plate cooling kits

productLines.name: Modular data centers (C500/C1000/C2000/C9000, Silicon Cube)
productLines.note: Micro, row-level, pool-level and containerized modular data center portfolio plus the vertical Silicon Cube facility design

facts.text: China's first national data center liquid cooling standard, GB/T 48023-2026 (Technical Specification for Cold-Plate Liquid Cooling Systems in Data Centers), released July 2026 with Sugon DataEnergy as chief drafting unit — effective February 1, 2027
Released C8000 V3.0 (April 2026) — MW-class phase-change immersion full-rack solution at >900 kW per rack
Launched the C7000-F, presented as China's first phase-change indirect liquid cooling data center solution

faq.q: What is Sugon DataEnergy's most powerful immersion system?
faq.a: The C8000 V3.0 (April 2026) — a phase-change immersion full-rack solution supporting >900 kW per rack with heat flux >200 W/cm² and PUE <1.04, billed as the world's first MW-class offering of its kind.

faq.q: Did Sugon DataEnergy write China's liquid cooling standard?
faq.a: It was chief drafting unit of GB/T 48023-2026 — China's first national standard for cold-plate liquid cooling systems in data centers, released July 2026 and effective February 1, 2027.

profiles.name: Inventec
profiles.tagline: Taiwanese electronics manufacturer (founded 1975, Taipei) whose data center solutions group builds NVIDIA MGX server and rack systems; its Artemis liquid-cooled rack line supports GB200/GB300 NVL72 and Vera Rubin NVL72 building blocks with rack-mounted, sidecar and row-based CDU cooling.

productLines.name: Artemis Rack (NVIDIA GB200 NVL72)
productLines.note: 48RU-class MGX rack rated max 125 kW for GB200 NVL72 building blocks; cooling options span rack-mounted, sidecar and row-based liquid cooling with an Inventec self-developed rack-mounted CDU, leakage detection and blind-mate NVLink cable cartridge and manifold.

productLines.name: Artemis II Rack (NVIDIA GB300 NVL72)
productLines.note: Rack rated max 136 kW for GB300 NVL72 building blocks; supports sidecar and row-based liquid cooling with leakage detection and blind-mate NVLink cable cartridge and manifold design.

productLines.name: Artemis III Rack (NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72)
productLines.note: 48RU NVIDIA MGX rack with 228 kW TDP for Vera Rubin NVL72 building blocks; 100% liquid-cooled compute and switch tray solution, sidecar/row-based cooling, 5000 A+ power busbar and a 3RU 19-inch 110 kW power shelf built from 6x 18.3 kW PSUs.

productLines.name: Liquid-cooled AI servers
productLines.note: P9000G7 and P5800G7 servers based on NVIDIA HGX B300 with both air and liquid cooling options, and the liquid-cooled P600G7 accelerated by NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPU, shown in the May 2026 press release.

facts.text: Showcased the Artemis III rack for NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72, liquid-cooled Intel Xeon 6 servers and a containerized data center solution at SC26 in a November 4, 2026 release.
Stated in its May 26, 2026 release that the Artemis III rack powered by NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 is in full production, ahead of COMPUTEX 2026 (June 2-5, Nangang Exhibition Center Hall 2).
Unveiled the Artemis III rack with 72 Rubin GPUs and 36 Vera CPUs at NVIDIA GTC 2026 in a March 10, 2026 release, alongside HGX B300 and HGX Rubin NVL8 servers.

faq.q: Which liquid-cooled racks does Inventec offer?
faq.a: Three NVIDIA MGX racks: Artemis rated max 125 kW for GB200 NVL72 with rack-mounted, sidecar and row-based cooling; Artemis II rated max 136 kW for GB300 NVL72; and Artemis III with 228 kW TDP for Vera Rubin NVL72, all with leakage detection and blind-mate manifolds.

faq.q: What is special about the Artemis III cooling design?
faq.a: Artemis III uses a 100% liquid cooling compute and switch tray solution served by sidecar or row-based cooling, with a blind-mate manifold, 5000 A+ current-rated power busbar and a 3RU 19-inch 110 kW power shelf made of 6x 18.3 kW PSUs.

faq.q: Does Inventec sell liquid-cooled servers too?
faq.a: Yes. Its 2026 releases list P9000G7 and P5800G7 servers based on NVIDIA HGX B300 with air and liquid cooling options, the liquid-cooled P600G7 with NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs, and liquid-cooled Intel Xeon 6 servers shown at SC26.

faq.q: Who is Inventec?
faq.a: Inventec was established in 1975 with its Taiwan headquarters in Shilin District, Taipei, and trades on the Taiwan Stock Exchange under stock code 2356; its data center solutions group covers servers, storage, racks, accessories and cooling.

profiles.name: Advantech
profiles.tagline: Advantech is a Taiwanese industrial computing and IoT platform maker (TWSE: 2395). For data centers it builds the SKYRack family of integrated rack solutions that combine compute and GPU nodes with networking and air-cooling or liquid-cooling options, including CDU-integrated configurations.

productLines.name: SKYRack AI
productLines.note: Integrated rack solution for AI training, inference and simulation, combining Intel Xeon and AMD EPYC servers, 2U/4U GPU servers based on NVIDIA MGX architecture, networking, and air-cooling or liquid-cooling options.

productLines.name: SKYRack SEMI
productLines.note: Rack-level solution integrating computing nodes, GPU nodes, networking and a cooling distribution unit (CDU); certified to SEMI S2 standards and configurable as a half rack or full rack for site-specific cooling and computing requirements.

productLines.name: Direct-to-chip integration and monitoring
productLines.note: Direct-to-chip cooling integrated into industrial computing platforms with thermal partner KEMMEC; the company says it is developing integrated monitoring combining wireless sensing with thermal management for liquid-cooling reliability and predictive maintenance.

facts.text: At COMPUTEX 2026 (booth K0603a, Nangang Exhibition Center, Taipei) Advantech showcased SKYRack SEMI, a rack-level solution integrating a cooling distribution unit (CDU), alongside SKYRack AI rack solutions for enterprise AI deployment.

An Advantech industry-focus article published October 28, 2025 positions SKYRack as integrated liquid-cooling infrastructure for high-density enterprise deployments, describing rack densities moving from approximately 20 kW air-cooled racks toward 50 kW and beyond, with direct-to-chip cooling integrated through partner KEMMEC.

faq.q: What is Advantech SKYRack?
faq.a: SKYRack is Advantech's family of integrated rack solutions. SKYRack AI targets AI training, inference and simulation with air-cooling or liquid-cooling options and supports NVIDIA MGX-based 2U/4U GPU servers; SKYRack SEMI integrates a cooling distribution unit (CDU) and is certified to SEMI S2 standards.

faq.q: Does Advantech build its own liquid cooling hardware?
faq.a: The company states it integrates advanced cooling technologies, including direct-to-chip cooling, into its industrial computing platforms through partnerships with thermal solution providers such as KEMMEC. It also says it is developing integrated monitoring solutions for liquid-cooling system reliability and predictive maintenance.

faq.q: What rack densities does Advantech target?
faq.a: In its 2025 liquid-cooling overview Advantech describes traditional air-cooled racks at approximately 20 kW and next-generation AI, HPC and hyperscale deployments at 50 kW and beyond, which is where its SKYRack liquid-cooling infrastructure is aimed.

faq.q: Who owns Advantech and where is it based?
faq.a: Advantech is listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange as TWSE: 2395. Its corporate press releases are datelined Taipei, Taiwan, and the company describes itself as a provider of IoT intelligent systems and embedded platforms.

profiles.name: IMMERSEKOOL
profiles.tagline: Korean manufacturer of liquid cooling connection components and systems for AI data centers, EV and power electronics: cold plates, OCP ORV2/ORV3 rack manifolds, EPDM hose kits and quick coupling modules for single- and two-phase direct liquid cooling, plus immersion chambers and built-to-order in-rack and in-row CDUs.

productLines.name: ORV3 DLC Manifolds
productLines.note: Blind-mate manifolds to OCP Open Rack V3.0 for high-density AI racks such as NVIDIA GB200 systems; AISI 303 stainless, maximum operating pressure 50 psi (3.45 bar), 10-65 C operating range, 5 mm nominal flow, up to 9 L/min per port, 100% helium-leak tested; an HPR variant serves racks above 100 kW.

productLines.name: DLC Cold Plates
productLines.note: Cold plates for NVIDIA H100 GPUs, Intel EGS and Birch Stream-AP (BHS-AP) platforms, AMD EPYC 9004/9005 series (SP5 socket), plus DIMM/memory plates, PSB (Power System Board) plates and custom IGBT plates; sold as kits with 3/8-inch EPDM hose and UQD04 couplings.

productLines.name: EPDM Hose Kits and Quick Couplings
productLines.note: EPDM hose kits up to 1-inch and 4-inch diameters with SUS304 stainless crimp sleeves (IMK02-IMK12 series); OCP-series quick couplings including BMQC, LQC, UQD, UQDB and FD83 plus DN3/DN8 auto couplings; 2D drawings and STEP CAD models published for UQD hose barb couplings.

productLines.name: Immersion Chambers and CDUs
productLines.note: Built-to-order immersion systems: single-phase immersion tanks with circulation and coolant distribution (CDU included) and two-phase immersion chambers with condenser and heat-exchanger structures; in-rack and in-row CDUs designed to customer rack and server configurations.

facts.text: Presented AI data center direct liquid cooling solutions and products at OCP Korea Tech Day 2026, held at COEX in Seoul on August 21, 2026.
Released 2D product drawings and 3D STEP CAD models of its OCP UQD hose barb coupling crimp sleeves for download on product pages to support customer design review.
Supplied its KLC TTV 2.0 thermal-performance verification solution for AI data center direct liquid cooling within Korea and exhibited at Data Center Korea 2026 at the aT Center (November 4-6, 2026).

faq.q: What does IMMERSEKOOL supply for AI data center liquid cooling?
faq.a: The company designs and manufactures cold plates, OCP and custom rack manifolds, EPDM hose kits and quick coupling modules for single- and two-phase direct liquid cooling, plus single- and two-phase immersion chambers and built-to-order in-rack and in-row CDUs.

faq.q: Which OCP rack interfaces does it support?
faq.a: Its manifolds comply with OCP Open Rack V3.0 using blind-mate quick disconnects (BMQC), with an HPR variant for racks above 100 kW such as NVIDIA GB200 systems; hose kits pair with UQD04 couplings, and ORV2 and ORV3 manifold variants are listed.

faq.q: What are the published ratings of its ORV3 manifold?
faq.a: The IMK-MAN-002 ORV3 manifold is AISI 303 stainless steel, rated to 50 psi (3.45 bar) maximum operating pressure, 10-65 C operating temperature, 5 mm nominal flow diameter and up to 9 L/min maximum flow per port, with 100% helium-leak testing.

faq.q: Does it serve markets outside data centers?
faq.a: Yes. The same component portfolio targets EV and power electronics cooling, including custom cold plates for IGBT modules, and its inquiry checklist asks for cooling group, heat load in kW, interface types and delivery country.

profiles.name: JONHON
profiles.tagline: JONHON is a Luoyang-based maker of optical, electrical and fluid connection products, listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange (002179) and controlled by AVIC. Its 2025 annual report names a liquid cooling solutions segment covering UQD/UQDB quick disconnects, cold plates, cooling chassis and coolant source units for data centers.
profiles.ownership: SZSE: 002179; controlled by Aviation Industry Corporation of China (AVIC)

productLines.name: UQD / UQDB quick disconnects
productLines.note: Fluid connectors named in the 2025 annual report: high-reliability UQD and UQDB series quick disconnects for computing, enabling tool-free, spill-free connection of server cold plates and coolant loops in data-center liquid cooling systems.

productLines.name: Mini-QDB / XBMC micro quick disconnects
productLines.note: Micro liquid-cooling quick disconnects for optical module cooling: Mini-QDB with maximum outer diameter 10.2 mm and XBMC with maximum outer diameter 9 mm, radial float of 0.5 mm, flow up to 0.9 L/min, dual seals rated for 1,500 mating cycles; sized for QSFP-DD, OSFP and XPO module formats.

productLines.name: Cold plates, cooling chassis and coolant source units
productLines.note: The 2025 annual report lists high-efficiency liquid cooling plates for computing, liquid cooling chassis, coolant source units and fluid transfer piping and assemblies; the company website describes data-center cooling systems supporting both cold-plate and immersion cooling.

facts.text: JONHON is acknowledged among the companies that provided feedback on the OCP Universal Quick Disconnect (UQD) Specification v2.0.0, dated September 22, 2026. The specification defines design and test criteria for supplier-interchangeable hand-mate and blind-mate (UQDB) liquid-cooling quick disconnects.

JONHON introduced the Mini-QDB and XBMC micro liquid-cooling quick disconnect series for cooling inside optical modules, with maximum outer diameters of 10.2 mm and 9 mm, radial float of 0.5 mm, flow up to 0.9 L/min, and a dual-seal design rated for 1,500 mating cycles, targeting QSFP-DD, OSFP and XPO module formats.

The 2025 annual report names a Liquid Cooling Solutions and Other Products segment listing UQD and UQDB series fluid connectors for computing, high-efficiency liquid cooling plates, liquid cooling chassis, coolant source units and fluid transfer piping, and records the creation of a dedicated liquid cooling business division.

profiles.ocp: Acknowledged for feedback in the OCP Universal Quick Disconnect (UQD) Specification v2.0.0 dated September 22, 2026, alongside Dell, Intel, Amphenol, Staubli and Parker.

faq.q: What liquid cooling products does JONHON make for data centers?
faq.a: Its 2025 annual report lists a liquid cooling solutions segment with high-reliability UQD and UQDB series fluid connectors for computing, high-efficiency liquid cooling plates, liquid cooling chassis, coolant source units and fluid transfer piping and assemblies. The company website data center section describes a cooling system built from fluid connectors, cold plates, piping and coolant sources, supporting both cold-plate and immersion cooling.

faq.q: Is JONHON involved in OCP liquid cooling standards?
faq.a: Yes. JONHON is listed among the companies acknowledged for feedback in the OCP Universal Quick Disconnect (UQD) Specification v2.0.0, dated September 22, 2026, which defines design and test criteria for interchangeable hand-mate and blind-mate (UQDB) quick disconnects used in data-center liquid cooling.

faq.q: What are the Mini-QDB micro quick disconnects?
faq.a: Mini-QDB and XBMC are micro liquid-cooling quick disconnects for optical modules, introduced in August 2026. The Mini-QDB has a maximum outer diameter of 10.2 mm and the XBMC 9 mm, with radial float of 0.5 mm, flow up to 0.9 L/min and a dual-seal design rated for 1,500 mating cycles, sized for QSFP-DD, OSFP and XPO module formats.

faq.q: Where is JONHON based and who controls it?
faq.a: JONHON is headquartered in Luoyang, Henan, China, and is listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange under code 002179. Its actual controller is Aviation Industry Corporation of China (AVIC), as stated in its 2025 annual report.

profiles.name: FRD
profiles.tagline: FRD (Shenzhen FRD Science & Technology, SZSE: 300602) is a Shenzhen-based maker of electromagnetic shielding and thermal management materials and devices, founded in 1993. Its thermal line spans liquid-cooling cold plates, heat pipes and vapor chambers

productLines.name: Server liquid cooling cold plates
productLines.note: Server liquid-cooling plates described in the 2025 annual report as eliminating cascading and increasing heat-exchange area for high-power chips, with single-point cold plates dissipating more than 800 W, used for liquid cooling of server and data-center compute chips with low energy consumption and low noise.

productLines.name: Heat pipe and vapor chamber cooling modules
productLines.note: Heat pipe and VC vapor chamber cooling modules for telecom and server equipment, covering whole-board, high-power and high-heat-flux applications; the annual report states FRD has co-developed 3D VC and VCE special-purpose radiators with customers.

productLines.name: Liquid Cooling Plate
productLines.note: Produced with two patented processes, air blowing with brazing and stamping with brazing, in automated production in Changzhou; patents CN 202011321551X and US 11975376B2; applied to power battery packs, energy storage battery packs, telecom equipment and 5G base stations.

productLines.name: Thermal interface materials
productLines.note: Self-developed range of 11 categories and more than 80 products providing total thermal solutions, with thermal conductivity grades from 1 to 120 W/mK and UL 94 V0 flammability recognition for Canada and the USA; graphite films reach up to 1,850 W/mK in-plane and 15 W/mK through-plane.

facts.text: The 2025 annual report, published on April 28, 2026, lists server liquid cooling among its product applications, describing cold plates that dissipate more than 800 W per point for server and data-center compute chips and heat pipe/VC cooling modules including co-developed 3D VC and VCE radiators.

FRD listed its Liquid Cooling Plate product line on its official website in September 2024, based on patented air-blowing-plus-brazing and stamping-plus-brazing processes with automated production in Changzhou and patents CN 202011321551X and US 11975376B2.

faq.q: What liquid cooling products does FRD offer for servers and data centers?
faq.a: Its 2025 annual report lists server liquid cooling products: cold plates that dissipate more than 800 W per single point, designed for liquid cooling of server and data-center compute chips with high efficiency and low noise, plus heat pipe and VC cooling modules for telecom and server equipment, including 3D VC and VCE radiators developed with customers.

faq.q: How are FRD liquid cooling plates manufactured?
faq.a: The company produces liquid cooling plates with two processes, air blowing with brazing and stamping with brazing, in automated production in Changzhou. The solution is based on patented technology under Chinese patent CN 202011321551X and US patent 11975376B2, with high thermal conductivity and temperature uniformity.

faq.q: What thermal materials does FRD provide alongside liquid cooling?
faq.a: FRD offers self-developed thermal interface materials in 11 categories and more than 80 products, with conductivity grades from 1 to 120 W/mK and UL 94 V0 recognition, plus graphite films with up to 1,850 W/mK in-plane and 15 W/mK through-plane conductivity, supporting total thermal solutions for electronics and servers.

faq.q: Where is FRD based and listed?
faq.a: FRD was founded in Shenzhen in 1993 and is headquartered there, with production bases in Shenzhen, Suzhou, Changzhou, Foshan and Vietnam. It is listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange under code 300602.

profiles.name: Chunqiu Electronics
profiles.tagline: Chunqiu Electronics (SSE: 603890) makes laptop structural modules and new energy vehicle parts. Through the 2026 acquisition of Danish liquid cooling company Asetek A/S it gained AIO liquid cooling modules and a restarting server liquid cooling business for data centers.
profiles.ownership: SSE: 603890; owns Asetek A/S via wholly owned subsidiary CQXA Holdings Pte. Ltd.

productLines.name: Asetek AIO liquid cooling modules
productLines.note: Liquid cooling modules comprising pumps, fittings, tubing and coolant, applied mainly to desktop systems and planned to extend to data-center liquid cooling per the 2026 interim report; Asetek supplies brands including Dell, HP, ASUS and NZXT and works with AMD and Intel on new product launches.

productLines.name: Emma V3 [Gen10] AIO architecture
productLines.note: Flagship AIO cooling architecture unveiled at COMPUTEX 2026 with an optimized 4 mm offset cold plate design, dual-offset layout and center-groove micro-channels; delivers 1.5 C lower thermal resistance and roughly 45 percent lower perceived acoustic volume than the previous generation.

productLines.name: Workstation liquid cooling for Xeon and Threadripper
productLines.note: Workstation cooling for Intel Xeon and AMD Ryzen Threadripper processors with full IHS coverage unlocking TDPs above 450 W, shown at COMPUTEX 2026; Asetek has worked on workstation cooling since 2021 and has integrated with Chunqiu for manufacturing scale in Asia.

facts.text: Asetek unveiled the Emma V3 [Gen10] next-generation AIO liquid cooling architecture at COMPUTEX 2026, with a 4 mm offset cold plate design and micro-channel tuning, and showed workstation solutions for Intel Xeon and AMD Ryzen Threadripper with full IHS coverage unlocking TDPs above 450 W, following its strategic integration with Chunqiu for manufacturing scale in Asia.

Chunqiu Electronics completed its full tender offer for Nasdaq Copenhagen-listed Asetek A/S: accepts representing 95.3 percent of shares (303,298,827 shares) were received by April 13, 2026, settlement occurred on April 21, 2026, compulsory acquisition of remaining shares followed, and delisting was approved. The offer price was DKK 1.72 per share, with total consideration capped at DKK 547,371,523.76.

The 2026 interim report states that Asetek has begun restarting its dormant server liquid cooling business and is engaging overseas customers, with Chunqiu combining Asetek data-center liquid cooling experience and its own manufacturing capability to re-enter the data-center liquid cooling market.

faq.q: What does Chunqiu Electronics do in data-center liquid cooling?
faq.a: Through its 2026 acquisition of Danish company Asetek A/S, Chunqiu Electronics gained liquid cooling modules built around pumps, fittings, tubing and coolant. Asetek has more than a decade of data-center liquid cooling experience, and the 2026 interim report states its dormant server liquid cooling business is restarting with overseas customers being engaged.

faq.q: How did the Asetek acquisition proceed?
faq.a: Chunqiu Electronics announced a voluntary cash offer in November 2025 through its Singapore subsidiary CQXA Holdings Pte. Ltd. at DKK 1.72 per share, capped at DKK 547,371,523.76 in total. Accepts reached 95.3 percent of shares by April 13, 2026, settlement was completed on April 21, 2026, followed by compulsory acquisition of remaining shares and delisting from Nasdaq Copenhagen.

faq.q: What are Asetek liquid cooling specifications?
faq.a: At COMPUTEX 2026 Asetek unveiled the Emma V3 [Gen10] architecture with an optimized 4 mm offset cold plate, dual-offset layout and center-groove micro-channels, delivering 1.5 C lower thermal resistance and about 45 percent lower perceived acoustic volume than the previous generation, plus workstation cooling for Xeon and Threadripper above 450 W TDP.

faq.q: Where is Chunqiu Electronics based and listed?
faq.a: Chunqiu Electronics (Suzhou Chunqiu Electronic Technology Co., Ltd.) is based in Kunshan, Suzhou, Jiangsu, China, and is listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange under code 603890. It was founded in 2011 and also owns Asetek A/S through its subsidiary CQXA Holdings Pte. Ltd.

profiles.name: DAYUAN
profiles.tagline: DAYUAN (Zhejiang Dayuan Pumps Industrial, SSE: 603757) traces its origins to 1990 in Wenling, Taizhou, Zhejiang, and makes residential, commercial and industrial pumps under the Dayuan and Xinhu brands. Its shield canned-motor pumps circulate coolant in liquid cooling systems for data centers, AI computing, energy storage and vehicles.

productLines.name: Xinhu shield liquid cooling pumps
productLines.note: Canned-motor shield pumps that circulate coolant for liquid cooling in data centers, AI computing, energy storage, hydrogen fuel cells, electric vehicles and wind power; the 2025 annual report states 7.5 kW to 37 kW models are finalized and in batch production, with 40 kW and above units in prototyping.

productLines.name: CDU core main pump
productLines.note: A 37 kW CDU core main pump completed review by a domestic customer and a North American customer as of the 2025 annual report disclosure date; the company works with Vertiv and Taiwan channel partners to bring the product into global AI compute cooling chains, with 380 V to 800 V power-side capability.

productLines.name: Fluorine pumps for immersion and phase-change cooling
productLines.note: Special-media fluorine pumps for immersion and phase-change liquid cooling, adapted to reduce cavitation and size and improve integration; micro pumps for edge AI device cooling are partially commercialized, supported by motor control algorithms and miniaturized electromagnetic design.

facts.text: The 2025 annual report, published April 24, 2026, states the 37 kW CDU core main pump completed review by domestic and North American customers, the 7.5 kW to 37 kW pump range is finalized and in batch production, and 40 kW and above models are in prototyping, with cooperation ties to thermal management vendors including Envicool, Vertiv, Foxconn Industrial Internet, Nidec, Jonhon and ZTE.

In 2025 the company hosted a liquid cooling ecosystem co-building summit with a 2026 market outlook for the AI computing sector and completed testing, sampling and certification of its shield liquid cooling pumps with computing-service customers, achieving initial deployments in new scenarios.

The company reported continued development of fluorine pumps for immersion and phase-change liquid cooling and commercialization of first micro pump products for edge AI device cooling, strengthening refrigerant-compatible materials selection and thermal-fluid simulation capabilities.

faq.q: What pumps does DAYUAN make for data-center liquid cooling?
faq.a: Its commercial business includes liquid cooling pumps based on Xinhu shield canned-motor pump technology, used to drive coolant circulation in data-center and AI computing liquid cooling systems. The 2025 annual report states 7.5 kW to 37 kW models are finalized and in batch production, with 40 kW and above products in prototyping and a 37 kW CDU core main pump qualified by domestic and North American customers.

faq.q: What is the Xinhu brand?
faq.a: Xinhu is DAYUAN's shield pump brand, widely used in hot water circulation, thermal-control liquid cooling, chemical and nuclear power industrial applications. The 2025 annual report describes it as heat-resistant, corrosion-resistant and stable-running, and states the company cooperates with thermal vendors including Envicool, Vertiv, Foxconn Industrial Internet, Nidec, Jonhon and ZTE.

faq.q: Does DAYUAN serve immersion cooling?
faq.a: Yes. The 2025 annual report describes special-media fluorine pumps for immersion and phase-change liquid cooling, adapted to address cavitation, size and integration challenges, plus micro pumps for edge AI device electronic cooling that are partially commercialized.

faq.q: Where is DAYUAN based and listed?
faq.a: DAYUAN is headquartered at No. 689 Xicheng Road, Zeguo Town, Wenling, Taizhou, Zhejiang, China, with production bases in Wenling and Hefei. It traces its origins to 1990 and is listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange under code 603757.
